parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban, custody rule, border/document friction or police profiling of trans people is documented; the record is largely silent on the traveller-facing axes A–C and H, and in a thinly-documented jurisdiction that silence cannot be read as safety. What is documented is Tier-3 exposure: 2024 reporting that LGBT people must conceal themselves to live and work, public expression constrained (state-cancelled LGBTQ event), an old but real record of violence against gender-nonconforming people (2011, including murder), and — the heaviest present signal — the government in January 2025 rejecting recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence and hate speech and to equalise the age of consent. That is state-tolerated impunity with no working recourse, i.e. societal hostility the traveller cannot remedy. The unequal age of consent (5–10 years, demonstrably enforced in the 2020 arrest) is a secondary LGB statute but a narrow real exposure where a trans visitor's relationship could be framed as same-sex. Lacking any documented universal-exposure or visitor-service discrimination showing, this sits below the 0.55 profiles and near the 0.45 tier.
